Source-to-detector baseline in kilometers
Neutrino energy in gigaelectronvolts

Unit-conversion and phase-factor parameter equal to the relativistic vacuum oscillation phase coefficient for the chosen units
derivation_notes: This is the standard two-flavor vacuum neutrino-oscillation probability obtained by evolving the two mass-propagation eigenstates with their relativistic phase difference and projecting onto the muon flavor. The parameter kappa_osc absorbs the conversion factors and the factor associated with the phase difference for L in kilometers, E_nu in gigaelectronvolts, and Delta_m2 in square electronvolts.

domain_mechanisms.description: an energetically allowed reaction or decay channel

scenario_text: A relativistic neutrino is produced in one flavor state and detected after vacuum propagation as a different flavor. The conversion probability is determined by coherent phase accumulation between two propagation components and their mixing. The benchmark predicts the instantaneous detection probability from independently sampled baseline, neutrino energy, mixing strength, and propagation-component splitting. Matter interactions and incoherent scattering are held absent.

derivation_notes: The monochromatic vacuum result can be rewritten as sin(2*theta)**2*(1 - cos(2*phi))/2 with phi = kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu. Averaging over a finite symmetric energy spread suppresses the oscillatory cosine contrast while leaving the incoherent mean 1/2 intact; using a Gaussian phase-smearing closure gives the dephasing factor exp(-phi**2), which recovers the parent in the narrow-spread limit.
change_summary: The sharp-energy assumption was relaxed to finite coherent energy spread or detector energy resolution, so the observed target is an energy-averaged vacuum oscillation probability rather than a single-phase sinusoid. This introduces L/E_nu-dependent peak washing and saturation toward the averaged value at large phase.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The neutrino is ultrarelativistic and has a sharply defined energy.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Wave-packet or detector-resolution induced averaging over nearby neutrino energies causes partial dephasing of the oscillation phase while preserving two-flavor vacuum mixing.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: When phase smearing is negligible, exp(-(kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu)**2) -> 1 and the expression reduces exactly to sin(2*theta)**2*sin(kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu)**2.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed mixing angle, the transition probability is a pure sinusoid in the single ratio Delta_m2*L/E_nu, so all maxima have the same envelope sin(2*theta)^2 and the same harmonic shape.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the sharply defined neutrino energy assumption by a finite energy-spread average of the oscillation phase, so the observed probability becomes the phase-averaged sinusoid with L/E_nu-dependent damping of the oscillatory term.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding theta and Delta_m2 fixed, increasing L/E_nu no longer only moves along one undamped sinusoid: oscillation peaks are progressively washed out and the curve bends toward the averaged value instead of retaining full-amplitude extrema.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the source/detector energy resolution or intrinsic energy spread is not negligible compared with the oscillation-phase variation across the sampled packet, especially at large L, large |Delta_m2|, or low E_nu where phase changes rapidly with energy.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, the same theta and Delta_m2 can produce nearly parent-like oscillations at modest L/E_nu but suppressed extrema at larger L/E_nu; in holdout, extending to larger phase or lower energy strengthens this dephasing trend rather than introducing a different mechanism.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: In the zero energy-spread or perfect-resolution limit, the phase average collapses to the parent vacuum formula exactly.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: finite-energy-spread dephasing in two-flavor vacuum oscillations
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Wave-packet or detector-resolution induced averaging over nearby neutrino energies causes partial dephasing of the oscillation phase while preserving two-flavor vacuum mixing.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the oscillatory contrast now decays with phase magnitude, creating a saturation toward the mixed average that depends jointly on baseline, energy, and mass splitting rather than a uniform amplitude rescaling or phase shift.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The neutrino is ultrarelativistic and has a sharply defined energy.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The neutrino remains in coherent two-flavor vacuum propagation but the detected probability is averaged over a finite nearby energy distribution, producing phase dephasing.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: When exp(-(kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu)**2) approaches 1, the child becomes sin(2*theta)**2*(1 - cos(2*kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu))/2 = sin(2*theta)**2*sin(kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu)**2.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: For fixed theta and Delta_m2, compare modest and large values of phase kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu. The parent gives the same oscillation envelope sin(2*theta)**2 at every maximum, whereas the child shows progressively reduced peak-trough contrast and saturation toward sin(2*theta)**2/2 as phase grows under finite energy smearing. This is a changed scored target mapping from the supplied inputs, not merely a hidden-trajectory modification.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both low-phase nearly undamped extrema and high-phase washed-out extrema across the same theta and Delta_m2 conditions: refitting theta changes all amplitudes uniformly, while refitting kappa_osc or Delta_m2 only repositions the oscillation phase. None of those parent parameters introduces the required phase-dependent damping toward the averaged plateau.

derivation_notes: The exact-energy parent is refined by approximating finite energy averaging as a saturation of the effective oscillation phase and decoherence kernel when the phase sensitivity to energy, proportional to kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu**2, becomes appreciable. This preserves the same inputs while modifying the scored probability itself, and it reduces continuously to the parent when the energy-spread effect is negligible.
change_summary: Changed the sharp-energy assumption to finite energy-resolution averaging in vacuum propagation. The oscillation phase and damping now saturate with increasing energy sensitivity, producing an E_nu-dependent curvature change even at fixed phase coordinate kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The neutrino is ultrarelativistic and has a sharply defined energy.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Finite source or detector energy resolution averages the vacuum oscillation probability over nearby energies, producing additional phase smearing whose strength scales with the energy derivative of the phase.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: When (kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu**2)**2 << 1, the saturation factor 1 + (kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu**2)**2 approaches 1 and the parent expression is recovered.

response_change.parent_relation: The oscillation kernel depends on a single phase variable x = kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu through (1 - exp(-x**2)*cos(2*x))/2, so all L and E_nu dependence collapses to one universal shape after scaling by sin(2*theta)**2.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the sharply defined-energy phase assumption by finite source energy spread, so the detected probability becomes an energy-averaged oscillation kernel. The mapping then depends on x = kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu and on the local phase-smearing scale induced by averaging over E_nu, changing the curvature and damping rate with E_nu rather than preserving one universal x-shape.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed theta and fixed phase coordinate x, lower E_nu shows stronger suppression of oscillation contrast than higher E_nu because the same x reached at different absolute energies corresponds to different sensitivity to energy averaging; the parent cannot reproduce this with one shared parameter set because it predicts identical scaled response for identical x.

A single refit of the parent's existing parameter set cannot reproduce this cross-condition contrast because its mapping is constrained to be a universal function of x alone. This refinement is admissible when energy spread is finite but not so large that the phenomenon becomes completely washed out; in the vanishing-spread limit the parent law is recovered.

evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The neutrino is ultrarelativistic and has a sharply defined energy.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite source spectral width and detector energy-bin averaging induce additional, phase-gradient-dependent smearing of the two-flavor vacuum oscillation pattern.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the sharp-energy idealization already implicated by the parent’s dephasing structure and replace it with explicit energy averaging of the vacuum transition probability. The parent response depends on L and E_nu only through a single central phase and its fixed analytic damping form, so after one global refit it cannot independently match both weakly smeared oscillations at small phase slope and more strongly flattened extrema at large phase slope if those arise from averaging over a finite energy interval. The concrete contrast is obtained by varying L/E_nu while holding theta and Delta_m2 fixed: for small kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu**2 the child and parent are close, but for larger kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu**2 the child shows stronger curvature reduction and peak/trough compression because different nearby energies contribute different phases. This is scientifically admissible in vacuum, preserves P(0)=0 and probability bounds, and remains even though no matter effects or incoherent scattering are introduced. The refinement changes the scored target mapping itself, not only an auxiliary latent trajectory.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Introduce a distinct relaxation, transient, oscillation, or frequency scale.

scenario_text: A relativistic neutrino is produced in one flavor state and detected after vacuum propagation as a different flavor. The conversion probability is determined by coherent phase accumulation between two propagation components and their mixing. The benchmark predicts the instantaneous detection probability from independently sampled baseline, neutrino energy, mixing strength, and propagation-component splitting. Matter interactions and incoherent scattering are held absent.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed theta and Delta_m2, the parent maps x = kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu to transition probability through one shared oscillatory kernel with dephasing controlled only by powers of E_nu, so the envelope and phase are fixed functions of L/E_nu.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the sharply defined neutrino energy assumption by finite source spectral width and detector bin averaging, so the scored probability becomes an energy-averaged vacuum probability over the observed E_nu. This changes how curvature with respect to L/E_nu depends on E_nu because averaging suppresses rapid oscillations more strongly when the local phase gradient across the energy window is large.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding theta and Delta_m2 fixed, increasing L or decreasing E_nu eventually flattens oscillation extrema faster than the parent’s single built-in dephasing law predicts; at shorter baselines or higher energies the child reverts toward the parent-like oscillatory shape.

activation_condition: Observable when the experimental energy spread or averaging window is finite and the phase varies appreciably across that window, i.e. when |d/dE_nu(kappa_osc*Delta_m2*L/E_nu)| times the fractional energy width is not small; negligible in the narrow-energy limit.
train_hidden_contrast: Within training, modest variation of L/E_nu already shows extra damping at larger phase slope; in holdout with larger L or smaller E_nu the same mechanism strengthens, causing stronger smoothing of oscillation peaks and troughs rather than a simple rescaling.
continuation_path: Recover the parent in the zero-width energy-distribution limit, where the averaging kernel collapses to a delta function at E_nu and the observed probability equals the unaveraged vacuum result.
